abstract: The haemodynamics of the uterine arteries and myometrium were assessed using Doppler ultrasound in forty consecutive patients requiring treatment for invasive mole and choriocarcinoma. The investigations were performed prior to the commencement of chemotherapy and the subjects followed prospectively. The Doppler waveforms from the uterine arteries were analysed using the pulsatility index. It was found that patients with a pulsatility index of 1.1 or less were significantly more likely to develop drug resistance than those with a higher value (P < 0.04). There was no significant association between the pulsatility index and metastatic disease or uterine bleeding. Five out of eight patients who developed drug resistance could have avoided initial inadequate treatment if the Doppler findings were included in the scoring system for selecting chemotherapy for these tumours. It can be concluded that assessment of the uterine arteries using the pulsatility index prior to the treatment of patients with invasive mole and choriocarcinoma is of help in predicting those who will develop drug resistance.
abstract_ja: 化学療法を要する侵入奇胎および絨毛癌の患者40例を対象に、子宮動脈および子宮筋層の血行動態をドップラー超音波検査で評価した。検査は化学療法開始前に行い、患者を前向きに経過観察した。子宮動脈のドップラー波形は拍動指数で解析した。拍動指数が1.1以下の患者は、それより高い患者に比べ薬剤耐性を生じやすいことが有意に示された(P<0.04)。拍動指数と転移性疾患や子宮出血との間に有意な関連は認められなかった。薬剤耐性を生じた8例のうち5例は、化学療法選択のスコアリングシステムにドップラー所見を含めていれば、初期の不十分な治療を避けられた可能性がある。侵入奇胎および絨毛癌患者の治療前に子宮動脈を拍動指数で評価することは、薬剤耐性を生じる患者の予測に有用であると結論される。
